title: Petra and the Deadline
premise: Kestrel Vasquez, a whistle-blower living under four names, is approached by a stranger named Petra who claims Kestrel once saved her life — a favor Kestrel has no memory of. As they investigate, Kestrel discovers the 'favor' was implanted: Petra is a handler from Halcyon, the black-ops training network that erased and rebuilt people like Kestrel, and the debt is a leash designed to drag Kestrel back into service before an extraction flight at dawn can carry evidence of Halcyon's crimes to journalists. Torn between loyalty to the found family of fellow escapees who sheltered them and the truth that will destroy that family's safety, Kestrel chooses truth, burns Halcyon's network from inside its own safehouse, and puts Petra — who defects at the last moment — on the dawn flight in their place.
about_author: Tamsin Underhill is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years writing security briefings before turning to fiction. She lives off-grid with two dogs and an unhealthy knowledge of border crossings.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Bag
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We meet Kestrel mid-ritual: checking exits in a Lisbon café, rotating identities, go-bag by the door. A small kindness to a stranger — buying coffee for a soaked woman named Petra — closes the chapter with unease when Petra says 'I remember you.' Emotional beat: vigilance cracked by longing to be known.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra finds Kestrel's safehouse and repays a debt: warning that someone is hunting them. She describes, in detail, a night in Marseille when Kestrel pulled her from a burning car — a night Kestrel cannot recall but whose details are perfect. Beat: vertigo; memory itself becomes untrustworthy.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Petra names her price: accompany her to a meeting in Porto or she stops protecting Kestrel. Kestrel refuses, then finds their fourth identity already burned — passport flagged, landlord questioned. Beat: the trap closing, choice disguised as choice.

chapters.title: The Family You Pick
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel flees to the one safe constant: Marisol, Dev, and Okonkwo, fellow escapees running a dive bar in Bilbao — the found family. Warmth, banter, and the first lie Kestrel tells them about why they've come. Beat: belonging sharpened by guilt.

chapters.title: Halcyon Days
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Flashback structure: Petra's own training under Halcyon — conditioning, loyalty drills, the erasure protocol called 'the Quiet Room.' We learn favors are engineered debts. Beat: horror reframing everything she told Kestrel as possibly scripted.

chapters.title: Porto, After Dark
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The meeting Petra demanded: a Halcyon quartermaster offers Kestrel reinstatement and hints their memories were edited twice. Kestrel plays along, pockets a keycard. Beat: cold competence masking terror.

chapters.title: What Marisol Saw
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol recognizes the keycard's logo from her own past and confronts Kestrel. Old wounds open: Kestrel never told the family how deep their Halcyon history ran. Beat: betrayal inside sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Extraction Flight
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, a former air-traffic analyst, decodes intercepted chatter: a dawn cargo flight carrying Halcyon's ledger — proof of every erased operative — leaving from a private strip near Biarritz. Whoever holds it owns the truth. Beat: a deadline becomes a countdown.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Currency
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra reports to her handler that Kestrel is compliant, then privately wavers — reviewing her own Marseille memory and finding a seam: a detail that couldn't have happened. Beat: the handler's leash beginning to fray.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel and Petra compare memories of Marseille and realize both were given versions of the same night — Halcyon manufactured their bond to make this mission feel personal. Rage, then resolve: use the fake bond as a weapon. Beat: grief transmuted into strategy.

chapters.title: The Bar Burns
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Halcyon cleaners hit the Bilbao bar; the family scatters, Marisol wounded. Kestrel realizes staying together makes them targets. Beat: found family tested by fire, literally.

chapters.title: Safehouse Protocol
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The survivors regroup in a coastal squat Kestrel prepped years ago. They plan the Biarritz raid: Dev on comms, Marisol forging credentials despite her injury, Okonkwo on overwatch. Beat: fragile unity forged into a crew.

chapters.title: The Handler's Offer
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra's handler reveals the endgame: Kestrel is to be Quiet-Roomed again after the flight, and Petra promoted into Kestrel's old identity. He hands her the syringe. Beat: complicity crystallizing into revolt.

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Using the Porto keycard, Kestrel enters Halcyon's Biarritz staging facility posing as returned asset 'Vasquez.' Corridors of familiar dread; a glimpse of the Quiet Room itself. Beat: walking back into the nightmare voluntarily.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra, inside as handler, watches Kestrel locate the ledger vault — and quietly reroutes a camera feed to cover them. First overt act of treason. Beat: loyalty shifting sides in real time.

chapters.title: Quiet Room
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel is caught and strapped into the erasure chair; the technician begins the wipe. Interleaved flashes of all four names, the family, the bar. Beat: identity stripped to its final ember.

chapters.title: Petra's Choice
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra kills the power, frees Kestrel, and confesses everything — including that some fragment of the Marseille rescue was real, buried under her programming. Beat: confession as liberation; the debt repaid in reverse.

chapters.title: Burn the Network
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Together they trigger the facility's failsafe: uploading the ledger to journalists while igniting the server farm and training records. Alarms, fire, the network eating its own memory. Beat: catharsis through destruction.

chapters.title: Dawn Run
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The chase to the airstrip as Halcyon remnants try to fly the last copy out. Dev jams comms; Okonkwo disables the plane; the ledger's only surviving copy is now theirs. Beat: the deadline met by seconds.

chapters.title: One Seat
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. One extraction seat remains on a journalist's charter. Kestrel gives it to Petra — the only witness Halcyon will hunt hardest — keeping the decoy drive themselves. Beat: sacrifice as the truest form of trust.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unpacked
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Weeks later: the ledger breaks globally, Halcyon operatives exposed, the family reconvening in a new bar in a new city. Kestrel arrives with the go-bag finally unpacked. Beat: home chosen, not hidden.

chapters.title: Postcard from Nowhere
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A postcard arrives, unsigned except a drawn kestrel: Petra, alive and free somewhere north. Kestrel pins it above the bar. Final beat: memory imperfect, family intact, truth survived.
